newsitem.title: UK: Future UK rate changes to be signalled by repo.
newsitem.headline: Future UK rate changes to be signalled by repo.

text.p: Any future changes in official British interest rates will be signalled by a change in the Bank of England's repo rate, a spokeswoman for the central bank said.
This follows changes to the way the Bank conducts daily money market operations which took effect on Monday.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George were due to begin their monthly monetary meeting at 1100 GMT.
A Reuters poll of City economists showed none expects any change in official rates from the present 6.0 percent.

In recent years, the Bank announced any changes in official rates by setting a new minimum lending rate for the day. It then provided liquidity to the money market by buying bills at a new dealing rate.
Under the new system of daily operations, the Bank states what its repo rate is -- 6.0 percent at present, the same as base rates -- and how much assistance it has provided.
But it does not disclose a dealing rate for its purchases of outright bills.
